senses.gloss: बण् बण् = rt. वण्, q. v.

बणिज् बणिज्, क्, m. (connected with the
Vedic पणि fr. rt. 2. पण्, q. v.; but in Ved. and later
Sanskrit often written वणिज्), a merchant, (कु-बणिज्,
a wicked merchant); a trader; the sixth of the astrono-
mical periods called Karaṇa, corresponding to the half
of a lunar day; (क्), f. trade, traffic.
—बणिक्-पथ,
अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘a trader's path or line,’ traffic, com-
merce; (अस्), m. a merchant.
—बणिक्-पुत्र, अस्,
m. a merchant's son, son of a trader, a young mer-
chant or trader; (ई), f. a merchant's daughter, a
young woman of the merchant class.
—बणिग्-बन्-
धु, उस्, m. ‘trader's friend,’ the indigo plant, Indi-
gofera Tinctoria.
—बणिग्-भाव, अस्, अम्, m. n. the
state of being a merchant, traffic, trade, commerce.
—बणिग्-वह, अस्, m. ‘carrying merchants,’ a camel.
बणिज्य, अम्, आ, n. f. (for बाणिज्य), trade, traffic.

बाणिज्य, अम्, n. merchandize, trade, traffic, com-
merce.
बण्ड बण्ड, अस्, आ, अम्. See वण्ड.

बाण बाण, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. बण् or
वण्, to sound; in the later language more usually
written वाण, q. v.), a reed-shaft, shaft made of a
reed, an arrow.
—बाण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. made
or consisting of reeds, reeden, reedy; (आन्), m. ‘con-
taining reed-shafts,’ a quiver; an arrow.

बाणिज बाणिज, अस्, m. (fr. बणिज्), a mer-
chant, trader; (also written वाणिज.)

बाणिजिक, अस्, m. a trader, merchant; a rogue,
cheat; submarine fire.
